title: Reversal, Momentum and Intraday Returns
one_line: In US stocks (1993-2014), momentum is a morning effect (first-2-hour momentum alpha 0.82%/month) and reversal an afternoon effect (last-2-hour reversal alpha 0.59%/month); both weakened in 2004-2014.

findings.statement: First 2 hours (9:30-11:30) momentum: 4-factor alpha 0.82%/month vs 0.36% conventional.
Last 2 hours (14:00-16:00) reversal: alpha 0.59%/month; first-2-hour reversal negative.
Last-2-hour reversal alpha fell from 0.96% (1993-2003) to 0.35% (2004-2014).

why.pattern: Information trading in the morning, liquidity trading in the afternoon.

reported_results.headline: In US stocks (1993-2014), momentum is a morning effect (first-2-hour momentum alpha 0.82%/month) and reversal an afternoon effect (last-2-hour reversal alpha 0.59%/month); both weakened in 2004-2014.

tradable_edge: Cross-sectional; index cousin = morning trend / afternoon mean reversion, already partly in specs.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
